candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p. 12 / PDF p. 16: identify adverse effects and provide medication education; monitor/evaluate medication therapy
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — pregnancy medication safety / lorazepam neonatal effects
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize neonatal sedation and withdrawal as potential effects of late-pregnancy lorazepam exposure and avoid overstating these risks as inevitable outcomes.

options.A: The newborn can develop sedation and/or withdrawal symptoms after late-pregnancy exposure
options.B: Every exposed newborn will have a major structural birth defect
options.C: Lorazepam exposure late in pregnancy has no reported neonatal effects
options.D: The only possible neonatal effect is hypertension without neurologic or respiratory symptoms

candidate.rationale: Current DailyMed labeling states that lorazepam use late in pregnancy can result in neonatal sedation, including respiratory depression, lethargy and hypotonia, and/or withdrawal symptoms such as hyperreflexia, irritability, tremor and feeding difficulty. Therefore A is correct. The other options are unsupported absolutes or contradict the current label.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Late-pregnancy lorazepam exposure can result in neonatal sedation and/or withdrawal symptoms.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings/Precautions — Neonatal Sedation and Withdrawal Syndrome: late-pregnancy use can result in sedation (respiratory depression, lethargy, hypotonia) and/or withdrawal symptoms; monitor exposed neonates
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A pregnant client taking lorazepam asks about possible neonatal effects of exposure late in pregnancy. Which response by the nurse is accurate?
